_about: EU decision trees for the Commission guidelines C/2025/5045 (applying from 15 January 2026). allOf nodes are lists of the annex conditions; a learner answers each. Conditions are paraphrased; read the official text for exact wording.

yes.why: The new site needs an initial or product-specific GMP inspection, so the change is Type II.
A site for a product made by a novel or complex process is Type II.

no.why: Adding or replacing a site for a manufacturing operation on the finished product is Type IB.

pass.why: Adding or replacing an immediate packaging site that meets all the conditions is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met, so the packaging site is treated like any other manufacturing site: Type IB.

pass.why: Adding or replacing a secondary packaging site that meets the conditions is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition is not met, so it is treated like any other manufacturing site: Type IB.

pass.why: Labelling is a secondary packaging operation; with the conditions met it is Type IA-IN.
pass.note: Simplified: the app treats a labelling-only site as a secondary packaging site.

fail.why: A condition is not met, so it is Type IB.

yes.why: A batch control site using biological, immunological or immunochemical procedures for a biological product is Type IB.

pass.why: A batch control site using physicochemical or microbiological procedures, with the conditions met, is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

tree.why: Imprinting is a manufacturing operation on the finished product, so a new site for it is Type IB.
tree.note: The guidelines have no separate entry for imprinting sites.

tree.why: Adding or replacing a sterilisation site for a packaging component is Type IB.

yes.why: For a biologic, a scale change without process change, such as duplicating a line, is Type IB.

no.why: A new line that changes the process of a biologic may significantly affect quality: Type II.

yes.why: A change that may significantly affect quality, safety or efficacy is Type II.

no.why: Sterile products cannot use the Type IA route for process changes. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).
no.note: Simplified: check whether your change is a site change (Q.II.b.1) or a process change.

yes.why: A new site for a biological active substance is Type II.
A new active substance site supported by an ASMF is Type II.
The new site needs a significant update of the active substance dossier: Type II.

pass.why: Adding or replacing an active substance site with the same route and specifications is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: Adding or replacing an intermediate site with the same route and specifications is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: A major change that may significantly affect quality, safety or efficacy is Type II.

pass.why: A minor change to the manufacturing process that meets every condition is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: A major change that may significantly affect quality, safety or efficacy is Type II.

pass.why: A minor change to the manufacturing process that meets every condition is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: A major change that may significantly affect quality, safety or efficacy is Type II.

pass.why: A minor change to the manufacturing process that meets every condition is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: A change that may significantly affect sterility assurance is Type II.

no.why: Sterile processes cannot use the Type IA route. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).
no.note: Simplified: the guidelines have no entry for depyrogenation alone.

yes.why: A change to sterilising filtration that may significantly affect sterility assurance is Type II.

no.why: Sterile processes cannot use the Type IA route. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).
no.note: Simplified: the guidelines have no entry for filters alone; most authorities treat sterilising filter changes cautiously.

yes.why: Introducing a non-standard terminal sterilisation method is Type II.

no.why: Changing the sterilisation method is a major process change: Type II.

yes.why: A batch size change needing a comparability assessment or a new bioequivalence study is Type II.
A scale change for a biologic without process change is Type IB.
A batch size change for a product made by a novel or complex process is Type II.

pass.why: A change up to ten times (or down to a tenth) that meets the conditions is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met; the batch size change is Type IB.

no.why: A change of more than ten times up or down is Type IB.

tree.why: A substantially different route of synthesis is a major change: Type II.

yes.why: A major change to the active substance process is Type II.

pass.why: A minor change to the active substance process that meets the conditions is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

tree.why: Redefining the starting material changes the part of the route described in the dossier: a major change, Type II.
tree.note: Simplified: the guidelines have no separate entry; the app follows common practice for starting material redefinition.

tree.why: A new reprocessing procedure changes the approved process and may affect quality: Type II.
tree.note: Simplified: the guidelines have no separate entry for reprocessing.

pass.why: Changes to imprints or markings, including inks, that meet the conditions are Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: Changes to embossing, debossing or other markings that meet the conditions are Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: Deleting an in-process control that may significantly affect quality is Type II.

pass.why: Deleting a non-significant or obsolete in-process control is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: Adding a new in-process control and limits is Type IA when the conditions are met.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: A composition change supported by a bioequivalence study is Type II.
An excipient change that may significantly affect safety, quality or efficacy is Type II.

pass.why: A minor quantitative adjustment that meets the conditions is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

comparable.why: Replacing an excipient with a comparable one with the same function is Type IB.

other.why: Other qualitative or quantitative changes are treated as major: Type II.
other.note: Simplified: the app treats any change that is neither minor nor a like-for-like replacement as major.

pass.why: Adding, deleting or replacing a colouring or flavouring component is Type IA-IN when the conditions are met.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: Increasing or reducing a colouring or flavouring component is Type IA when the conditions are met.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

tree.why: A new strength is an extension of the marketing authorisation, not a variation.

pass.why: A change within the approved acceptance criteria (tightening) is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: An update to comply with an updated Ph. Eur. general monograph is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

no.why: A change outside the approved acceptance criteria is Type II.

yes.why: Deleting an attribute that may significantly affect quality is Type II.

pass.why: Deleting a non-significant or obsolete attribute is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: Adding a new attribute with its procedure and criteria is Type IA when the conditions are met.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met (for example the new test is for an impurity or dissolution). A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: An update to comply with an updated Ph. Eur. general monograph is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: Replacing or substantially changing a biological, immunological or immunochemical procedure is Type II.

no.why: Other changes to an analytical procedure are Type IB.

pass.why: A minor change to an approved procedure that meets the conditions is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met, so it is an other change: Type IB.

no.why: Other changes to an analytical procedure, including replacement, are Type IB.

yes.why: Introducing a biological, immunological or immunochemical procedure is Type II.

no.why: Introducing or replacing an analytical procedure is Type IB.

yes.why: A biological, immunological or immunochemical procedure is Type II.

no.why: Adding or revising an analytical procedure is Type IB.

pass.why: Deleting a procedure when an alternative is authorised is Type IA.

fail.why: The condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: Changing the analytical procedure for an in-process control is Type IA when the conditions are met.
pass.note: Changes to excipient test methods are under Q.II.c instead; the app uses the in-process control entry.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: Introducing or changing a biological procedure for a starting material, reagent or intermediate is Type IB.

pass.why: Other changes to a procedure for a starting material, reagent or intermediate are Type IA when the conditions are met.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: Changing the composition of the container for a sterile liquid is Type II.

pass.why: For solid forms, a change in container composition that meets the conditions is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

no.why: For semi-solid and non-sterile liquid forms, a change in container composition is Type IB.
A less protective pack, with storage or shelf-life changes, is Type II.

yes.why: A new container type for a sterile product is Type II.

no.why: A change in shape or dimensions of the container for a sterile product is Type IB.

yes.why: A major change to an integral device part that may affect delivery, quality, safety or efficacy is Type II.

no.why: Adding or replacing a device part without significant effect is Type IB.
no.note: The app maps dose-controlling packaging to the integral medical device entries in Q.IV.

yes.why: A new container type for a solid form is Type IB.

pass.why: For solid forms, a change in container composition that meets the conditions is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

no.why: A less protective pack is Type II.

yes.why: For non-sterile liquids, a change in the composition of the container or closure is Type IB.

no.why: A less protective pack is Type II.

yes.why: Shape or dimension changes of the container for a sterile product are Type IB.

pass.why: Shape or dimension changes for a non-sterile product that meet the conditions are Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: A new pack size within the approved range is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

no.why: A new pack size outside the approved range is Type IB.

pass.why: A change to the immediate packaging of a solid form that meets the conditions is Type IA.
pass.note: Simplified: the app treats a desiccant as part of the immediate packaging.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: Blister to blister, with equivalent material and stability data started, is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

no.why: A less protective pack is Type II.

pass.why: A change to secondary packaging that is not less protective is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met (for example the packaging protects the product). A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).
fail.note: If storage conditions or shelf life must change too, add that change (Q.II.f.1).

pass.why: A change to packaging not in contact with the product that affects the product information is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: The condition is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: A change to packaging not in contact with the product, with no effect on the product information, is Type IA.

fail.why: The condition is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

pass.why: For an immediate-release film-coated tablet with real-time data under the approved protocol, the extension is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met (for example the product is not an immediate-release film-coated tablet); a real-time extension is Type IB.
fail.note: Simplified: the guidelines list Type IB for extensions after first opening or reconstitution; the app applies Type IB to other real-time extensions by default.

yes.why: An extension based on extrapolation in line with the stability guidelines is Type IB.

no.why: An extension based on extrapolation or modelling not in line with the guidelines is Type II.

pass.why: Reducing the shelf life as packaged for sale is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA-IN is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).
fail.note: A reduction caused by stability problems may also need an investigation and a different procedure; discuss with the authority.

pass.why: A change to the approved stability protocol is Type IA when the conditions are met.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

yes.why: A change in storage conditions of a biological product is Type II.

no.why: A change in storage conditions is Type IB.

yes.why: Under an approved qualification protocol, a new in-house reference standard for a biological product needs no variation.
Replacing the reference standard with comparability results available is Type IB.

no.why: Replacing the reference standard without an approved protocol is Type II.
The reference standard entries cover biological products; for chemical products a new lot of an in-house standard qualified under GMP needs no variation.
no.note: Simplified: if the dossier itself changes, classify that change instead.

tree.why: Adding or modifying a therapeutic indication is Type II.
Changing the population or posology of an indication based on new data is Type II.
tree.note: Posology changes without an indication change come under C.4 (also Type II).

tree.why: Changes to the product information based on new quality, preclinical, clinical or pharmacovigilance data are Type II.

yes.why: Implementing wording agreed by the authorities, exactly and with agreed translations, is Type IA-IN.

no.why: Agreed wording that needs minor assessment (for example translations not yet agreed) is Type IB.
A safety update based on new data the authorities have not yet assessed is Type II.

yes.why: Implementing wording agreed by the authorities, exactly and with agreed translations, is Type IA-IN.

no.why: Agreed wording that needs minor assessment (for example translations not yet agreed) is Type IB.
A safety update based on new data the authorities have not yet assessed is Type II.

tree.why: Deleting a therapeutic indication is Type IB.
tree.note: For deleting other claims, check C.4.

yes.why: Implementing the outcome needs new data: Type II.
Implementing the agreed outcome with exactly the agreed wording is Type IA-IN.

no.why: Agreed wording that needs minor assessment is Type IB.

yes.why: A generic, hybrid or biosimilar following the reference product, with new data needed, is Type II.

no.why: A generic, hybrid or biosimilar following the reference product, with no new data, is Type IB.

tree.why: An editorial change to the product information on its own is Type IB by default.
tree.note: In practice editorial corrections are usually included with the next procedure that changes the product information.

tree.why: A change to the labelling or package leaflet not connected with the SmPC is notified under Article 61(3), not as a variation.
Introducing a post-approval change management protocol (PACMP) is Type II.

pass.why: A change made fully under the PACMP, which set Type IA, is notified within 12 months.

fail.why: The PACMP conditions are not met, so the change goes in its normal category without the protocol.
fail.note: Classify the change itself in its own entry.

pass.why: A change made fully under the PACMP, which set Type IA-IN, is notified immediately.

fail.why: The PACMP conditions are not met, so the change goes in its normal category.
fail.note: Classify the change itself in its own entry.

IB.why: A change made under the PACMP, which set Type IB, is notified as Type IB.

tree.why: A variation submitting a study, such as a bioequivalence study, is Type II.
A new master cell bank changes a biological starting material and may significantly affect quality: Type II.
tree.note: Simplified: the guidelines have no separate entry for master cell banks.

yes.why: A new working cell bank under an approved qualification protocol needs no variation; it is covered by the quality system.

no.why: Without an approved protocol, a new working cell bank is filed as Type IB (unforeseen change).

pass.why: A minor process change that meets the conditions is Type IA.

fail.why: A condition for Type IA is not met. A change that is not Type IA or Type II is a Type IB by default (Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 1234/2008).

no.why: A new resin, step or column for a biological active substance is a major change: Type II.

tree.why: Changing a virus removal or inactivation step is a major change: Type II.
A transfer of the marketing authorisation to another holder is a separate transfer procedure, not a variation (national procedures for nationally authorised products).

pass.why: A change in the name or address of the holder, which stays the same legal entity, is Type IA-IN.

fail.why: A new legal entity is a transfer, not a variation.
